issues.description: The problem statement's UML defines Farm.animals as a List<Animal>, but elsewhere in the same problem statement the textual instructions require the aggregation to be realized using a Set (HashSet) to enforce uniqueness. This inner-artifact contradiction leaves students unsure whether to implement animals as a List or a Set.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the contradiction in the problem statement: either change the UML to show a Set<Animal> (preferred, since the text emphasizes uniqueness) or revise the textual instructions to accept a List. Update the UML and all textual references so they consistently require the same collection type.

issues.description: The provided reference solution implements Farm.animals as a List (ArrayList) while the problem text explicitly requires using a Set implemented with a HashSet to ensure unique animals. This mismatch can confuse students comparing the solution with the assignment text and may cause tests or expectations about uniqueness to differ.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the assignment text by changing the Farm implementation to use a Set<Animal> and initialize it as a HashSet in the no-argument constructor. Alternatively, if List is intended, update the problem statement to remove the Set/HashSet requirement and clarify that duplicates are allowed.

issues.description: The collection type used to represent Farm.animals is inconsistent across artifacts. The UML in the problem statement declares animals: List<Animal> (problem_statement.md lines 16-21), but the textual instructions later explicitly require a Set backed by a HashSet for uniqueness (problem_statement.md lines 108-111). The solution implementation uses a List (ArrayList) for the animals field (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java lines 9-13). This mismatch (List vs Set/HashSet) refers to the same conceptual entity (the Farm's collection of animals) using different type identifiers and will confuse students about the required data structure.
issues.suggestedFix: Choose a single, consistent collection type for Farm.animals across all artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement UML to require a Set (and keep the textual description), then change the solution/template to declare private Set<Animal> animals and initialize it with new HashSet<>(), or (B) change the textual instruction to request a List if lists are intended. Prefer option (A) if uniqueness is a requirement: replace List with Set in UML and update solution/template to use Set<Animal> animals = new HashSet<>();.
